# Frost protection

A clear, still night in April is the dangerous one. I watch the evening forecast and, when the temperature is expected to fall below two degrees, cover the young plants with horticultural fleece held down by stones. Pots of seedlings come inside to the shed. Blossom on the apricot tree gets a double layer.

Water the soil in the afternoon: damp soil keeps its heat longer than dry soil. Uncover in the morning once the ice has melted, otherwise the plants cook under the fleece. A max-min thermometer by the greenhouse gives the real figures.

Keep a roll of fleece by the door all spring.
